description: Compare the LIVE market rate distribution now vs ~1/2/4 weeks ago for a product and state. Returns now/then min, median, max, count plus the median and min delta and a direction (down/up/flat). Bounded by data retention — if no comparable historical snapshot exists, then is null with an explanatory note. Use this to show how rates have moved recently.

since.description: How far back to compare against. Defaults to "1w".

state.description: US state code (2-letter, e.g., CA, TX). Required.

name: get_rate_delta

direction.description: Direction of the median move: 'up', 'down', or 'flat'.

median_delta_pct.description: Change in median APR, in percentage points (0.023 = about 2 basis points). Negative means rates fell.

min_delta.description: Change in the lowest published APR, in percentage points. This can move very differently from the median.

data_source.description: Internal backing store that served this query ('clickhouse'); operational detail, not something to report to the user.

note.description: Plain-English interpretation of the numbers above, already phrased for the user; quote it rather than re-deriving the comparison.

now.description: Current market snapshot for this product and state.

as_of.description: Timestamp of the most recent rate in the current snapshot.

count.description: Number of live offers behind the current snapshot.

max.description: Highest APR in percent currently published.

median.description: Median APR in percent currently published; the right number for 'what rates are today'.

min.description: Lowest APR in percent currently published — a single best deal, not a typical rate.

product_type.description: Loan or deposit category this result covers, e.g. 'mortgage', 'auto_loan', 'heloc', 'savings'.

state.description: Two-letter US state code the result is scoped to (e.g. 'CA'). Null means the result was not filtered by state.

then.description: Snapshot at the start of the window, for comparison against `now`.

count.description: Number of offers behind the earlier snapshot. This is often far smaller than now.count because history is retention-bounded, so treat the comparison as indicative.

max.description: Highest APR in percent at the start of the window.

median.description: Median APR in percent at the start of the window.

min.description: Lowest APR in percent at the start of the window.

window.description: Lookback period used for the comparison, expressed as a short duration string such as '4w', '90d', or '180d'.
